parts:
Dear authors,

I'm using MCDS to analyse a multi-species survey (birds) in five differen=
t land use types. I'll need individual species densities for each one of =
the land uses, which is quite complicated because of the minimum number o=
f observations to have a god fit, but I'm using a Global detection probab=
ility since the land uses are all 'open areas'. I'm also post-stratiying =
by Stratum (my land use types). It is working well, however for some spec=
ies I got the following message 'Warning: Maximum probability of detectio=
n is greater than one: invalid model fitted'. I couldn't find any topic o=
n the list about this except for another message in the Archives with no =
answer=E2=80=A6 I've tried Google with no luck as well=E2=80=A6. Why did =
I get these messages? When I look at the histograms of distance distribut=
ions it looks Ok, and for some of the species I got this message I have a=
large number of observations=E2=80=A6. I would be very grateful if you c=
ould help me!

Thank you very much!

Kind regards,
Graziela

ent land use types. I'll need individual species densities for each one o=
f the land uses, which is quite complicated because of the minimum number=
of observations to have a god fit, but I'm using a Global detection prob=
ability since the land uses are all 'open areas'. I'm also post-stratiyin=
g by Stratum (my land use types). It is working well, however for some sp=
ecies I got the following message 'Warning: Maximum probability of detect=
ion is greater than one: invalid model fitted'. I couldn't find any topic=
on the list about this except for another message in the Archives with n=
o answer=E2=80=A6 I've tried Google with no luck as well=E2=80=A6. Why di=
d I get these messages? When I look at the histograms of distance distrib=
utions it looks Ok, and for some of the species I got this message I have=
a large number of observations=E2=80=A6. I would be very grateful if you=
could help me!
Are you using adjustment functions and covariates? If you are it is the =

likely source of error. Adjustments are multipliers of the baseline key =

function. It is possible that for particular covariate values the=20
key*(1+adjustments) is >1. This constraint is not implemented in the=20
fitting but after fitting it checks to make sure for each observation=20
the predicted probability is not >1. Personally I've never been a fan=20
of fitting adjustments as well as covariates from a philosophical=20
standpoint and became even more convinced when I realized that p>1 was=20
possible.
